You are one of several subagents migrating a Python script (using python-jose JWT, HS256) to pure Node.js ESM. Shared context and rules:

- All generated code lives under `/output` (create dirs as needed). Library files in `/output/lib/`, entry file `/output/test17.mjs`. ALL files use `.mjs` suffix, ESM only (`import`/`export`; `require`/`module.exports` forbidden).
- ZERO external npm deps. No imports except local `.mjs` files (paths must include the `.mjs` suffix). Node built-in globals like `Buffer`, `process`, `console` are fine WITHOUT import. STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: importing or using `node:crypto` in any way (no createHmac/createHash/etc.) — SHA-256/HMAC must be pure-JS implementations.
- The original Python behavior to match (verified against a compiled executable):
  - JWT header is exactly `{"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}`; payload JSON serialized compact with Python `json.dumps(separators=(',',':'))` semantics INCLUDING `ensure_ascii=True` (non-ASCII chars escaped as `\uXXXX`, e.g. `héllo` -> `h\u00e9llo`, CJK chars -> `\u4e2d\u6587`). Escape set like Python json: `"` -> `\"`, `\` -> `\\`, control chars `\n \t \r \b \f` short forms, other chars < 0x20 as `\u00XX`, chars >= 0x7f... actually Python ensure_ascii escapes ALL chars >= 0x80 as `\uXXXX` (surrogate pairs for astral chars); 0x7f DEL is NOT escaped. Byte order of object keys = insertion order.
  - Decoded payload is printed as a Python dict repr, e.g. `{'info': 'hello', 'iat': 1786345209}`. Python str repr rules: prefer single quotes; if the string contains a single quote but no double quote, use double quotes; if it contains both, use single quotes and escape `'` as `\'`. Backslash -> `\\`, `\n` -> `\n` escaped as `\\n`, `\t`->`\\t`, `\r`->`\\r`; non-printable chars as `\xXX`/`\uXXXX`; printable non-ASCII (e.g. `é`, `中`) printed literally. Integers printed plain.
  - Token printed on its own line, then the dict repr on the next line. Exit code 0.

FIXED INTERFACE CONTRACT (other agents implement/consume exactly these — do not deviate):
- `./sha256.mjs`: `export function sha256(bytes /* Uint8Array */) -> Uint8Array` (32-byte digest)
- `./hmac.mjs`: `export function hmacSha256(keyBytes /* Uint8Array */, msgBytes /* Uint8Array */) -> Uint8Array`
- `./base64url.mjs`: `export function b64urlEncode(bytes /* Uint8Array */) -> string` (no padding); `export function b64urlDecode(str) -> Uint8Array`
- `./pyjson.mjs`: `export function pyJsonDumps(value) -> string` (Python json.dumps compact + ensure_ascii semantics for the subset: strings, numbers, booleans, null, arrays, plain objects)
- `./pyrepr.mjs`: `export function pyRepr(value) -> string` (Python repr for the same subset; dicts as `{'k': v, ...}` with `, ` separator, strings per rules above, numbers plain, True/False/None for booleans/null)

Also support `--data=VALUE` inline form. Support args in any order. Help text format (argparse standard):
```
usage: PROG [-h] --data DATA --verify_iat {true,false}

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --data DATA
  --verify_iat {true,false}
```

  secret = "secret"
  payload = {"info": args.data, "iat": int(time.time())}
  token = jwt.encode(payload, secret)          # default HS256
  print(token)
  verify_iat = args.verify_iat == 'true'
